newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended generally firmer, with shorter maturities gaining relative to the long end despite news the Swiss National Bank left its discount rate unchanged at 1.50 percent at its weekly policy-setting meeting.
In grey market activity, Rabobank set a 100 million Swiss franc issue maturing December 30, 2003. Traders said that the spread between yields and swaps has narrowed of late.

One trader saw Rabobank as relatively expensive for the market. The issue, with a 3.75 percent coupon priced at 102.25, was quoted on a screen by lead manager Merrill Lynch at minus 2.40/2.20, yielding 3.77 percent.
Another bank compared the Rabobank issue to an issue by top borrower Deutsche Ausgleichsbank which was yielding 3.88 percent for a seven-year issue.
According to the lead, however, "Rabo is a very well-liked borrower, and whenever it comes, it is expensive."
The grey market was seen as tough for new issues.
"The market is at the moment very difficult. Swap rates have come down sharply, and bonds have not reacted in the same way," one bond source said.
"The spread between yields and swaps has gotten very narrow," he added.
Dec conf futures CONFZ6 up nine at 114.20
Dec comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 up 28 at 109.88.
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESZ6 up five at 98.06.
